name: Guam

law.summary: EPA Region 9 issues the permits. No Guam statute or rule requiring operators to tell the public of a spill was found; Guam EPA posts beach advisories and, rarely, special advisories after bypasses. GWA reports spills to Guam EPA and EPA under a federal court order.

regulator_report.deadline: 24 hours oral, 5 days written (EPA permit standard condition)

bills_and_cases: US v. Guam Waterworks Authority (D. Guam): stipulated order and 2011 court order (search_only)

erule.notes: All 17 are the Navy's Apra Harbor system (GU0110019), not Guam Waterworks as assumed; GWA's five systems are registered with no events.

statewide_feed.notes: Covers one federal system only; not island-wide.

beaches.program: Guam EPA Beach Watch (BEACH Act), 43 beaches weekly

barriers.what: GWA spill reports go to regulators only
Guam EPA GIS server reset or 503 from this machine
barriers.note: may be an outage or geo-block

subscriptions.name: Guam EPA beach report contact
subscriptions.what: Beach report questions; no list found

readiness.rationale: Weekly official beach advisories in an ArcGIS layer (once reachable) plus the Navy's SOBE events; nothing from the island's main utility.

owner_questions: Retry the Guam EPA GIS server from the GitHub Actions runner before deciding the first feed?
surprise: Guam's 17 SOBE events are the Navy's Apra Harbor wharves, not Guam Waterworks; the utility serving most of the island has filed no overflow reports with EPA's tool.
